domain_setting: An everyday financial world of a neighborhood bank, card terminal, cash desk, household budget, bills, savings, loans, currency exchange and stock trading. Keep payment objects, bank services, household expenses, borrowing and business finance visually distinct.
recurring_scale_anchors: 304x192 card, grounded objects on a pale counter or desk with an elliptical contact shadow
Banknotes, receipts, cards and invoices are blank paper shapes with non-letter squiggles only; no readable text, numerals, logos or currency glyphs
Coins use simple ridged circular silhouettes without numeric denominations
Use a consistent slate-blue bank interface and warm paper, copper and gold financial objects

polysemy_resolution_table.check (payment) / cheque (uk spelling): A paper payment instrument handed to a cashier; not the verb meaning stop or prevent.
polysemy_resolution_table.pin: A confidential card PIN represented only by a card reader and covered keypad; not a fastening pin and no digits shown.
polysemy_resolution_table.tip: A gratuity left beside a restaurant bill; not the pointed end or a helpful hint.
polysemy_resolution_table.balance: The amount remaining in a bank account, represented by a statement or ledger and available funds; not a weighing scale or physical equilibrium.
polysemy_resolution_table.bank: A financial institution with teller counter and secure deposit drawers; not a riverbank.
polysemy_resolution_table.deposit: Money placed into a bank account, shown moving into a bank drawer or account; not sediment or a rental security deposit.
polysemy_resolution_table.transfer: Movement of funds between financial accounts; the neighboring transfer-money entry shows the concrete act of sending money.
polysemy_resolution_table.withdrawal: Cash removed from a bank account at an ATM; not retreat, leaving a group, or an emotional withdrawal.
polysemy_resolution_table.go out: Money leaving a household or business budget as an expense in this finance lesson; not a person leaving home socially.
polysemy_resolution_table.interest: Money charged on borrowed funds or earned on savings; not curiosity or attention.
polysemy_resolution_table.interest rate: The proportionate borrowing or savings charge represented by a share of principal, without numerals or written percent signs.
polysemy_resolution_table.save: Set money aside in a savings jar or account for later; not rescue, preserve, or save a file.
polysemy_resolution_table.change money: Exchange one currency for another at a currency counter; not making change after paying cash.
polysemy_resolution_table.finance: Management and movement of money for an organization, represented by ledger, funds and cash flow; not curiosity.
polysemy_resolution_table.stock exchange: A financial marketplace where company shares are bought and sold, represented by traders, chart shapes and certificates without letters.

contrast_notes.cash / coins / notes / currency / money: Show cash as a ready-to-spend collection, coins as round metal pieces, notes as blank folded paper money, currency as visibly different banknote and coin designs, and money as a broad mixed pile of coins and notes.
contrast_notes.cash register / receipt / bill / invoice: Separate the checkout drawer, proof of completed payment, itemized amount owed, business invoice sent to a buyer, and professional service charge.
contrast_notes.credit card / debit card / pin: Credit card is a borrowed-spending card, debit card is linked to a bank balance, and PIN is the private keypad interaction; omit text and digits.
contrast_notes.bank / bank account / bank statement / b: Distinguish institution, personal account container, account activity summary, remaining funds, cash machine, phone-based service, and browser-based service.
contrast_notes.deposit / withdrawal / transfer / transf: Show funds entering an account, cash leaving an ATM, funds moving between account containers, a person initiating that movement, and account spending below zero with a shortfall cue.
contrast_notes.bill / budget / expenditure / go out / o: Differentiate amount owed, planned income-versus-spending envelope, total spending, money leaving the budget, a one-time disbursement, and public revenue collected for civic services.
contrast_notes.bank loan / loan / debt / get into debt: Show bank loan as an institutional lending desk, loan as money temporarily lent, debt as money still owed, getting into debt as obligations accumulating, and mortgage as a house-secured long-term loan.
contrast_notes.interest / interest rate: Interest is the actual extra money earned or owed; interest rate compares that amount against borrowed or saved principal.
contrast_notes.break even / make a loss / income / econ: Show equal revenue and costs, costs overtaking revenue, money received from work or business, and broad business activity contracting across multiple firms.
contrast_notes.exchange rate / change money / stock exc: Keep currency conversion at a bank exchange counter, physical currency swapping in change money, and share trading at a stock exchange.
